description: A 2-year-old fractured her leg at a Georgia daycare that broke state teacher:child ratios. How a Bright from the Start complaint can help prove negligence.
shortAnswer: If your child was injured while in daycare, it is possible that the fault can be traced to the childcare center's negligence in following state standards. If so, you may have a strong case. To prove negligence, the incident must be investigated, which is why it is very important that you file a complaint with Bright from the Start.

faq.q: What teacher-to-child ratios must licensed Georgia daycares follow?
faq.a: Bright from the Start requires licensed daycares to follow specific teacher:child ratios that vary based on the age of the children: under 1 year or under 18 months if not walking = 1:6; 1 year and walking = 1:8; 2 years = 1:10; 3 years = 1:15; 4 years 1:18; 5 years = 1:20; 6 years and older = 1:25.

faq.q: What makes a daycare injury case strong?
faq.a: My client had a very strong case. However, this was not due primarily to the seriousness of the injury, but rather to the ability to clearly prove that the injury was a result of negligence on the part of the daycare.

faq.q: Do a daycare's past violations matter in an injury claim?
faq.a: Bright from the Start records showed 11 previous violations of the staff:child ratio standards alone. This proved a pattern of negligence on the part of the daycare. In court, a jury would likely see this pattern as grounds for punishing the daycare by awarding punitive damages on top of the general damages.

faq.q: What should I do after filing a complaint about my child's daycare injury?
faq.a: After filing a complaint, get in touch with an attorney. Maybe the daycare is clearly at fault and in violation of state standards. Or maybe your daycare is exempt from licensure and is not required to follow state standards.
